Name: 300 Swedish Birds
MetaDescription: The checklist for birders in Sweden. Tick off species, log where and when you saw them, identify birds by their song and compete with friends. Free, in your browser.
Eyebrow: The checklist for birders in Sweden
Headline: Every bird you see in Sweden, in one list.
Lede: Tick off species as you see them, note where and when, and watch your year list grow. Free, on your phone and your computer.
MockLabel: Example of the app: a year list with 87 of 300 species, a bird identified by its song and a new species added.
SearchLede: Look up any of the over 2,000 species in the catalogue, read about it and hear its song. No account needed.
SearchPlaceholder: Search by name, like blackbird or Turdus
SearchReportHint: Create a free account and the sighting is waiting there, ready to save.
SearchFailed: Couldn't load the species. Try again in a moment.
FeaturesLede: Built by birders for birders in Sweden: quick to use in the field, and with all the details when you get home.

Showcase.title: A list for every goal
Showcase.text: Start from the 300 most common Swedish birds, or make your own list for the year, the garden or a single trip.
points: Ready-made list of the 300 most common species
Your own lists, as many as you like
Progress for every list at a glance

Showcase.title: Where and when, kept for you
Showcase.text: Each sighting keeps its date and position and is placed in the right county and municipality automatically.
points: Position from your phone or a pin on the map
Count, age, sex and a comment when you want them
Export everything as CSV or JSON

Showcase.title: Hear a bird you don't know?
Showcase.text: Record up to ten seconds of song and get the most likely species, with how sure the guess is. Pick one to report it.
points: Suggests species that occur in Sweden at this time of year

Showcase.title: Bird together with friends
Showcase.text: Set a period and a species list, invite your friends and follow who gets furthest.
points: Your own rules: period, list and number of participants
Optionally the first to reach a number of species wins
Invite friends or open it to everyone

Showcase.title: Report birds in a chat
Showcase.text: Connect Claude or another AI assistant and talk to your lists: tell it what you saw, or ask how your year is going.
points: Report sightings and ask about your lists in plain words
You approve the assistant and can disconnect it whenever you like
Connect it under Settings › Manage API keys

Showcase.title: Your list on the big screen
Showcase.text: Every checklist has a page of its own to share. Put it on the TV at the bird club or send it to a friend: it keeps itself up to date as you add species.
points: One link per list, no account needed to look
Made for a TV, works on a phone too
Shows species and dates, never where you saw them

More.title: Know the bird
More.text: Photos and a short description from Wikipedia for every species.

More.title: Works offline
More.text: Report sightings without a connection; they are sent when you are back online.

More.title: Phone and computer
More.text: The same lists everywhere, in the browser you already have.

HowTitle: Up and running in a minute

Steps.title: Create an account
Steps.text: All you need is an email address. It's free.

Steps.title: Choose a list
Steps.text: Start with the 300 most common species, or make your own.

Steps.title: Tick off birds
Steps.text: Report what you see. Your lists and statistics update right away.

Faq.a: No. 300 Swedish Birds is free to use. You can support the project with a donation if you like.
The ready-made list has the 300 most common birds in Sweden. Your own lists can include any of over 2,000 species in the catalogue.

Faq.q: Do I need to install an app?
Faq.a: No. 300 Swedish Birds runs in the browser on your phone, tablet and computer.

Faq.q: Can I get my data out?
Faq.a: Yes. Download a list as a spreadsheet (CSV) or all your data at once, whenever you like.

Faq.q: How reliable is the sound identification?
Faq.a: It is a suggestion, not a certain identification. It works best with a clear recording of a singing bird, close by.

CtaText: Free, and ready in a minute. The next bird you see could be the first one on it.
